name: ASPCA: farm animals
beneficiaries_note: Our build: US hens and sows under state laws and higher-welfare purchases.
summary: The ASPCA's farm animal welfare team, a small part of its $422m spending in 2025 (about $8m with its share of public education, our judgment), lobbied against federal and state rollbacks of the laws that keep hens out of cages and sows out of crates, and pushed shoppers, farmers and producers toward higher-welfare products and in-ovo sexed eggs. Defending the laws also keeps their compliance costs (the regulator's figure for California's Proposition 12, about $300 million a year net of retailers' margin), which at the site's values outweigh the animals' gain, so the result is below zero, about −0.001 years of healthy life per $1,000. Both are small per dollar: the defence is shared with a coalition in which the ASPCA's own spending (about $1.5m of lobbying and outreach) is a small part, its 2025 work removed only a share of the override risk, and its large reserves make the next dollar worth less than the average. The biggest uncertainties are that cost, the share of the risk the opposition removed, how many hens and sows would go back into cages if the laws fell, the coalition's total spending and the share of the ASPCA's policy spending that goes on farm animals, which the accounts don't give; the result is mostly uncertainty, spanning several orders of magnitude, and both branches are discounted for missing outcome data.

sections.title: In chicken pain days
sections.explainer: charityevals' standard step for every animal model. The shared SAD figures are Ambitious Impact's, which count each species' pain as a share of a person's with its own species weights. Here those weights come out and Rethink Priorities' go in, so every species is counted in days of a chicken's disabling pain. How a chicken compares with a person is the one animal slider.

rows.explainer: Media $81,594, mailings $39,805, publications $7,772, grants for lobbying $216,967, direct contact $784,388, rallies and lobby days $122,772, other $597,316: every issue, from puppy mills, horse slaughter, housing and telehealth to the farm laws.

rows.label: Share of the ASPCA's 2025 lobbying spent defending farm-animal laws
rows.explainer: Our judgment: Schedule O names, for 2025, three California puppy-mill laws, New York's pet-shop law, the SAFE Act on horse slaughter, housing, telehealth and disaster bills beside the farm preemption fight. 40%, 25% to 60%.

rows.label: Defence work not reported as lobbying, 2025
rows.explainer: Our judgment: the farm team's coalition work, farmer outreach (the farmers' views it gathered on Proposition 12 before the July 2025 House hearing) and communications on the defence that fall outside the lobbying definition; a few staff's time at about $150,000 each with overheads, the anchor of facts/aspca.json. $0.8m, $0.3m to $2m. The rest of the farm budget is the market branch, the Crate Free Illinois grant and the opposition to faster slaughter lines; the last two won nothing in 2025 and add no modelled outcome.

rows.label: State repeal fights won, as a multiple of the federal defence
rows.explainer: Our judgment from the ASPCA's review of the year: repeal bills in Colorado and Michigan (whose laws cover over 12 million birds) 'failed to gain any traction', so they were at small risk; Arizona's governor vetoed a repeal but the law was already delayed to 2034, outside the years counted; Nevada passed an emergency suspension. 1.02, 1 to 1.1.

rows.label: Market: hen-years a year in the shift the ASPCA's guide, farmer work and in-ovo advocacy touch (before what would have happened anyway and others' share)
rows.explainer: Our judgment. The ASPCA's Shop With Your Heart guide steers shoppers and buyers to eggs, chicken, pork and beef under meaningful welfare certifications, it works with independent higher-welfare farmers, its Fund to End Factory Farming gave $160,305 to seven projects in 2025 (community and environmental groups opposing factory-farm pollution), and it championed in-ovo sexed eggs, on sale in 15 states from 2025 (Form 990 Schedule O, line 4c). It publishes no count of animals affected. We express it as hens moved from cages to cage-free housing: 300,000 hen-years a year (about 0.1% of the flock), 50,000 to 2 million.

source.title: ASPCA, Announcing: 2025 Fund to End Factory Farming grantees
source.quote: $160,305 in grant funding for seven critical projects

rows.label: Side effect: caged eggs and crated pork sold elsewhere, as a share of the animals' gain
rows.explainer: The shared figure: when buyers or states stop taking caged eggs or crated pork, some of it is sold elsewhere for a while (Norwood and Lusk's 0.91 eggs per egg not bought leaves about 9%), and dearer cage-free eggs move a few buyers to chicken meat. A harm, so negative: −10%, from −25% to 0.
